rv.q: It’s a clever icebreaker before the show settles into its main task: tracing Guinness’s life from his childhood, born to an unmarried mother and never knowing his father, to his late-career triumph as George Smiley in the BBC’s Tinker Tailor Soldier Spy. Along the way, Soanes morphs through more than 30 characters.

As the story unfolds, these coverings are pulled away, sending small plumes of dust into the air, as if the memories have been lying dormant, waiting to be disturbed. It is a simple idea, but a really effective one. Zeb Soanes delivers something really special in his performance as Alec Guiness, and the many figures who helped shape his career.
